recipes.name: The Sims Special
ingredients: For the Molten Mac and Cheese
Reserved chilled stovetop mac and cheese
2 cans (28 oz) hand crushed San Marzano tomatoes
1 sprig large basil + more to garnish
8 oz low moisture mozzarella cheese, thinly sliced
48 oz vanilla ice cream, slightly softened
48 oz strawberry ice cream, slightly softened
48 oz chocolate ice cream, slightly softened
instructions: For the Mac and Cheese
Line a small bowl with plastic wrap.
Combine the water and milk in a saucepot. Add the pasta and bring the mixture to a boil. - 1 ½ cup water - 1 cup whole milk - 8 oz dried macaroni
Cover and cook until the pasta is cooked and has absorbed most of the liquid, about 6-8 minutes.

Add the cheese and stir to combine. Turn off the heat and cover the pot. Let the macaroni and cheese sit for 5 minutes until all the cheese has melted. - 4 oz american yellow cheese shredded - 6 oz sharp cheddar cheese shredded
Pour the pasta into the prepared bowl and refrigerate until firm, about 30 minutes.
Take the solidified mac and cheese out of the refrigerator and unmold.
For the Molten Mac and Cheese
Combine the water and milk in a sauce pot. Add the pasta and bring the mixture to a boil. - 1 ½ cup water - 1 cup whole milk - 8 oz dried macaroni
Cover and cook until the pasta is cooked and has absorbed most of the liquid, about 6-8 minutes.

Add the cheese and stir to combine. Turn off the heat and cover the pot. Let the macaroni and cheese sit for 5 minutes until all the cheese has melted. Keep warm until ready to use. - 8 oz american yellow cheese shredded - 4 oz sharp cheddar cheese shredded
Meanwhile, combine the butter and breadcrumbs in a small bowl. - 2 tbsp unsalted butter melted - 3 oz panko bread crumbs
Coat the exterior of the reserved mac and cheese in the breadcrumb mixture. - Reserved chilled stovetop mac and cheese
Coat the original bowl with a generous layer of oil or nonstick spray. Place the now-breaded mac and cheese back in the bowl. - Oil

Scoop out about 2 cups of the chilled mac and cheese to form a crater in the middle. Place a small metal bowl inside of the crater to help maintain its shape. - Reserved chilled stovetop mac and cheese
Bake the mac and cheese bowl in a preheated 400°F oven until crispy, about 15-20 minutes.
Remove the insert bowl and fill the cavity with the fresh, molten mac and cheese. Run a spatula along the outside of the crispy mac and cheese to help it release.
Invert the mac and cheese onto a plate. Garnish with parsley and serve immediately. - To garnish: parsley leaves
For the Aubergine Parmesan
Line three large rimmed baking sheets with paper towels.
Slice the aubergine into ½ inch slices. - 1 large or 2 medium aubergines (eggplants)

Place the aubergine slices on the prepared sheet trays. Sprinkle the slices with salt on both sides. Stack the trays one over the other to weigh down the slices. Top the final tray with another (unlined) sheet tray. Weigh down the stack of sheet trays with a heavy-duty casserole dish. Let the aubergine slices sit for 1 hour. - As needed kosher salt
Begin heating the oil in a large dutch oven. - 3 tbsp olive oil
Add the onion and cook for 3-4 minutes or until slightly tender. Add the garlic and cook for an additional 1-2 minutes or until fragrant. - 1 yellow onion - 4 cloves garlic

Add the crushed red pepper flakes, dried oregano, and tomato paste. Stir well to incorporate and cook for 1-2 minutes more. - ¼ tsp crushed red pepper flakes - ½ tsp dried oregano - 2 tbsp tomato paste

Add the crushed tomatoes and basil sprig. Reduce the heat to medium-low. Cover and allow the sauce to cook for 30-45 minutes. - 2 cans (28 oz) hand crushed San Marzano tomatoes - 1 sprig large basil + more to garnish

Prepare three large shallow dishes. One with the flour, salt, and pepper, another with the eggs, and the final dish with the breadcrumbs and dried herbs. - 2 cup all purpose flour - 1 tsp kosher salt - 1 tsp freshly ground black pepper - 4 eggs beaten - 2 cup breadcrumbs - 1 tsp dried basil - 1 tsp dried parsley - ½ tsp dried oregano
Dredge the aubergine slices in the flour mixture, then egg, and finally the breadcrumbs. Transfer the dredged slices to a rack placed in a large rimmed baking sheet until ready to fry.
Preheat a large skillet with ½ inch of oil to 375°F. - As needed fry oil
Working with 2 or 3 slices at a time, fry each side for 3-4 minutes or until golden brown on both sides.
Transfer the fried aubergine to a large rimmed baking sheet lined with paper towels. Let cool to room temperature.

In a large heavy-duty casserole dish, start assembling the aubergine parmesan. Start with a layer of sauce, then a layer of aubergine, followed by a layer of low moisture mozzarella and parmesan cheese. Repeat this layering process until the casserole dish is filling. Make sure to finish with a layer of fresh mozzarella slices. - 8 oz low moisture mozzarella cheese thinly sliced - 4 oz parmesan cheese grated - 6 slices fresh (high moisture) mozzarella
Cover the casserole dish with a layer of aluminum foil and bake at 375°F for 30-40 minutes.
Uncover the casserole and bake for another 30 minutes. Increase the temperature to 425°F and bake for an additional 10-15 minutes or until browned and bubbling.
Allow the aubergine parmesan to cool for 20-30 minutes before serving.
For the Base Cake
Prepare an 8-inch cake pan with nonstick spray and a parchment round. Preheat the oven to 375°F. - Non spray

Add the eggs and sugar to the bowl of a stand mixer fitted with a whisk attachment. Whip the egg/sugar on high speed until thickened, pale, and fluffy, about 4-5 minutes. - 2 large eggs - 50 g granulated sugar

Sift in the flour, baking powder, cocoa powder, and salt onto a piece of parchment. Tip the sifted ingredients into the bowl of whipped eggs and fold to incorporate. - 30 g all purpose flour - ½ tsp baking powder - 20 g cocoa powder - ¼ tsp kosher salt
Pour the melted butter down the side of the bowl and once again, fold to incorporate. - 20 g unsalted butter melted + cooled
Pour the batter into the prepared cake pan.
Transfer the cake to the preheated oven and bake for 10-12 minutes or until cooked through and pulled away from the sides of the pan.
Let cool at room temperature.
For the Italian Meringue
Add the egg whites and cream of tartar to the bowl of a stand mixer fitted with a whisk attachment. - 4 egg whites - ⅛ tsp cream of tartar

In a medium saucepot, combine the sugar and water. Bring the mixture to 240°F. Stir the mixture just until it comes to a boil, then cover with a lid to remove any sugar granules stuck to the side. - 225 g granulated sugar - 45 g water
Meanwhile, begin whipping the egg white until they are white and frothy.

Once the sugar syrup is ready, carefully pour the syrup into whipping egg whites on medium speed. Increase the speed to high and continue mixing until the meringue is thick, glossy, and has returned to room temperature, about 15-20 minutes.
For the Baked Alaska
Prepare a medium bowl (with an 8-inch diameter) with plastic wrap with a generous overhang.
Pour the vanilla ice cream into a bowl of a stand mixer fitted with a paddle attachment. Mix the ice cream until softened, about 2-3 minutes. - 48 oz vanilla ice cream slightly softened
Add the vanilla ice cream to the prepared bowl. Freeze the bowl for 1 hour.

Repeat the mixing and layering process with the strawberry and chocolate ice cream. Make sure to freeze the ice cream insert in between ice cream additions. - 48 oz strawberry ice cream slightly softened - 48 oz chocolate ice cream slightly softened
Once the bowl is filled with all three ice cream flavors, add the base cake. It should fit perfectly into the bowl. - Base cake
Freeze the ice cream insert overnight.
Unmold the ice cream insert onto a turntable, cake-side down. Place the turntable on a metal sheet tray if your work surface is not stone or inflammable.
Working quickly, spread the Italian meringue onto the ice cream insert. Smooth out the exterior using a bowl scraper or mini offset spatula. - Italian Meringue
Add the alcohol to a small pot and bring to a simmer. Carefully, ignite the alcohol using a torch and ladle the flaming alcohol over the meringue. - 12 oz high proof (80) alcohol
Allow the flame to extinguish itself and then serve immediately.
